hero.title: Panambur
hero.description: Experience the golden sands, exciting water sports and mesmerising sunsets at Panambur Beach, one of the most popular beaches in Mangalore.

overview.title: About Panambur Beach
overview.p1: Panambur Beach is widely regarded as one of the cleanest and safest beaches in India. Located adjacent to the New Mangalore Port, this picturesque destination attracts thousands of tourists every week for its lively beach carnival atmosphere, thrilling water sports, and tranquil sunset views over the Arabian Sea.
overview.p2: Known for hosting the world-famous International Kite Festival, Panambur boasts certified lifeguards, jet skiing, camel & horse rides, and an array of beachside shacks serving fresh Mangalorean seafood and snacks.
highlights: Cleanest Beach with Lifeguards
Jet Ski, Parasailing & Boat Rides
Famous International Kite Festival
Beach Shacks & Seafood Delicacies

hero.title: Tannirbhavi
hero.description: A tranquil haven of pristine golden coastline, whispering Casuarina pine groves, and peaceful Arabian Sea sunsets.

overview.title: About Tannirbhavi Beach
overview.p1: Tannirbhavi Beach is celebrated for its natural simplicity, uncrowded sands, and adjacent verdant pine forest tree park. Reached either by road or a picturesque river ferry from Sultan Battery, it offers a quieter and more intimate beach retreat.
overview.p2: Walk under the shaded pine canopy, sit on the sun-warmed sands listening to roaring surf, or take the iconic boat ferry crossing Gurupura River for an unforgettable coastal journey.
highlights: Whispering pine tree groves and eco-friendly tree park
Scenic river ferry crossing from Sultan Battery jetty
Peaceful, clean coastline perfect for nature lovers and families
Spectacular unobstructed sunset vistas across the horizon

hero.title: Kadri Manjunath
hero.description: A sacred 10th-century heritage shrine renowned for bronze deities, eternal Gomukha spring water ponds, and Buddhist-Hindu cave heritage.

overview.title: About Kadri Manjunath Temple
overview.p1: Perched on the verdant Kadri Hill, the Kadri Manjunath Temple dates back to at least 1068 CE. Originally affiliated with Vajrayana Buddhism before becoming a principal Shaivite shrine, it houses one of the finest bronze statues in India—the seated Lokeshwara bronze cast by King Kundavarma.
overview.p2: Behind the main sanctum, natural natural springs flow through seven stone ponds called Gomukhas. Devotees perform ablutions in these crystal streams before climbing further to the ancient Pandava Caves carved high on the hill.
highlights: One of the oldest temples in South India dating back over 1,000 years
Magnificent Trilokyanatha Lokeshwara bronze sculpture from 968 CE
Sacred Gomukha natural hillside spring ponds with healing water
Ancient Pandava caves and scenic Kadri Park adjoining the premises

hero.title: Light House
hero.description: A British-era stone watchtower and lush hilltop garden offering 360-degree panoramic views of the city skyline and Arabian Sea.

overview.title: About Light House Hill Garden
overview.p1: Erected in the 18th century by Haider Ali, the historic watchtower at Light House Hill stands gracefully over the downtown heart of Mangalore. Surrounded by flower beds, shaded benches, and gentle sea breezes, it serves as an urban sanctuary for locals and tourists.
overview.p2: From the crest of the hill, visitors can gaze across the sparkling Arabian horizon, trace ships moving into port, and witness radiant sunsets painting the coastal sky in crimson and gold.
highlights: Historic 18th-century watchtower built by Haider Ali
Sweeping panoramic vistas of the Arabian Sea and city skyline
Peaceful landscaped botanical gardens with shaded pergolas
Prime central location close to St. Aloysius Chapel & city landmarks

hero.title: Netravati
hero.description: The sacred lifeline of coastal Karnataka, famous for scenic boat rides, tranquil backwaters, and breathtaking bridge sunsets.

overview.title: About Netravati River
overview.p1: Originating in the Western Ghats of Kudremukh, the Netravati River winds majestically through Dakshina Kannada before uniting with the Gurupura River and flowing into the Arabian Sea. It forms Mangalore's most scenic waterfront estuary.
overview.p2: Along its banks, fishermen cast traditional nets while visitors take soothing boat rides, relish fresh coastal seafood, and watch twilight reflections shimmer across the tranquil waters.
highlights: Magnificent tidal river and backwaters flowing into the Arabian Sea
Idyllic sunset vantage points along Ullal and Jeppinamogaru riverbanks
Fresh river fish cuisine and waterfront dining nearby
Historic bridges offering iconic railway and highway river vistas

hero.title: Sultan
hero.description: A historic miniature fortress and watchtower constructed by Tipu Sultan, offering ferry crossings and panoramic waterfront trails.

overview.title: About Sultan Battery
overview.p1: Built out of black stone in 1784 by Tipu Sultan, Sultan Battery was designed to prevent British warships from sailing up the Gurupura River into Mangalore. Resembling a miniature fort with mounting places for cannons, it offers an imposing view of the river mouth.
overview.p2: Today, it is a bustling recreational hub where travelers can climb the old watchtower, take scenic motorboat rides, or board the river passenger ferry to reach the golden beaches of Tannirbhavi in minutes.
highlights: Historic 18th-century black stone defense watchtower built by Tipu Sultan
Cannon vantage points overlooking the Gurupura River inlet
Popular ferry terminal connecting directly to Tannirbhavi Beach
Water sports, jet ski rides, and scenic waterfront promenade
